key_insight: A lightweight AgentSpeak autonomous agent can be embedded on a low-resource two-wheeled robot to make real-time navigation decisions from onboard sensors, enabling autonomous maze exploration without continuous external control.
problem_solved: How to enable independent, low-latency decision-making on resource-constrained embedded robotic platforms so they can operate reliably in dynamic environments without constant remote control.
method: Implement a compact AgentSpeak agent runtime on the robot and map sensor inputs to agent beliefs/percepts.
Use a lightweight perceive–believe–plan–act loop for navigation and obstacle avoidance to keep reasoning and memory footprints small.
Deploy on a two-wheeled robot and evaluate maze exploration performance and resource usage (latency, CPU/RAM, success rate).
impact: Shows a practical path for deploying symbolic agent architectures on edge robots, reducing dependence on remote computation and improving responsiveness — useful for practitioners designing low-power, autonomous systems and for trade-off analysis between behavior complexity and hardware limits.
visual_elements: System block diagram: AgentSpeak runtime ↔ sensors ↔ actuators (highlighting on-board compute constraints)
Perceive–Believe–Plan–Act flowchart annotated with example sensor-to-belief mappings
Photo/illustration of the two-wheeled robot navigating a maze with trajectory overlay
Performance/resource chart: success rate, navigation latency, CPU/RAM/energy usage across trials
paper_title: Embedding Autonomous Agents in Resource-Constrained Robotic Platforms
paper_authors: Negar Halakou, Juan F. Gutierrez, Ye Sun, Han Jiang, Xueming Wu
